title: ORTHO32
approach: SystemVerilog scalar pipeline, TLA+ specifications, Lean 4 developments, and a matrix-oriented instruction extension.
problem: Predictable execution and explicit architectural state transitions.
scope: FPGA and ASIC paths are under development. Published proofs concern their formal models; this site does not certify fabricated silicon or guarantee every AI workload completes in 768 cycles.

title: ORTHO Host
approach: C#/.NET 8 Worker Service with named-pipe IPC, a capability broker, routing, and service registration.
problem: A host boundary for device, build, and inference services.
scope: Repository implementation and documentation are available. No independent production, security, or hardware certification is asserted here.

title: ORTHO API
approach: Python FastAPI bridge to ORTHOHost via named-pipe IPC.
problem: A versioned service interface for clients.
scope: Requires the host service. Public code is not evidence of a deployed production API or verified end-to-end hardware integration.

title: ORTHO Java SDK
approach: Typed Java APIs for devices, tensor jobs, execution traces, and verification results, with a simulator transport.
problem: Stable application-facing interfaces over the ORTHO system contracts.
scope: Simulator tests do not establish FPGA or ASIC performance. Hardware transport support must be checked against the current project documentation.

title: ORTHO MCP
approach: An AWK stdio MCP server with explicit JSON-RPC method dispatch.
problem: A compact tool surface for ORTHO clients.
scope: The current README describes an AWK implementation. This is not a claim of broad IDE compatibility or independent security certification.

title: ORTHO AI Gateway
approach: M/MUMPS routines implementing request state, routing, provider calls, streaming events, IPC, and usage records.
problem: An explicit inference request path across the ORTHO stack.
scope: The public README describes the current M/MUMPS core. Website chat is a separate, restricted local-model gateway; it does not expose administrative tools.

title: ORTHO Desktop
approach: Swift on Windows with OpenSwiftUI, Win32/Direct2D, a routing shell, and ORTHOMessages.
problem: A user interface that communicates through ORTHOHost rather than directly with hardware.
scope: Integration depends on host services and Windows components. Public source does not imply a finished installer or validated hardware product.

title: ORTHO Isolation
approach: A layered design for root of trust, a minimal hypervisor, hardware data plane, formal isolation, and signed control commands.
problem: Separate tenant workloads from security-critical management functions.
scope: Architecture and proof materials require independent assessment. No completed security evaluation or deployed isolation guarantee is claimed.

title: Sovereign Kernel
approach: Fortran 2018 and MLIR-oriented kernel work targeting ARM64 SVE2, x86 AVX-512, and PTX.
problem: Explicit compute paths with accompanying formal-method and attestation materials.
scope: Claims in repository documentation have not been independently recompiled or benchmarked as part of this website update.

title: Jacobian Formal
approach: Lean 4 and Mathlib infrastructure for formal derivatives, Jacobian matrices, and related algebraic obligations.
problem: Investigate formal components of the Jacobian Conjecture.
scope: The README calls this partially verified infrastructure. This page does not claim a proof of the general Jacobian Conjecture.

title: LiquidLean
approach: m4 templates, Higher-Order Constraints, Liquid Haskell, and Haskell implementation work.
problem: Explore constraint systems and polynomial algebra with explicit proof obligations.
scope: Research status is determined by the current obligations and audits. No general resolution of an open conjecture is claimed by this website.

title: LiquidOrder
approach: LCF-style proof certificates, predicate ordering, fixed-point reasoning, and a preregistered research protocol.
problem: Keep theorem construction controlled while exploring proof-producing automation.
scope: Conditional theorems and empirical tracks have separate scope. Planned or gated experiments are not completed results.

title: DMZ over F₂
approach: Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization work on an algebraic characteristic-two reduction.
problem: Study the stated algebraic construction with machine-checkable definitions.
scope: A characteristic-two construction does not by itself establish the full analytic DMZ theorem or physical black-hole entropy predictions.

title: CARRY
approach: Rust execution with a Prolog logic kernel and braid-based transition tracking.
problem: Explicit state progression and transition evidence.
scope: Formal or topological descriptions do not establish security or correctness for arbitrary agent actions.

title: Foundry Intel
approach: Proof-lab, policy, agent-runtime, and append-only record tooling.
problem: Organize obligations and execution evidence in a documented workflow.
scope: Public repository claims are scoped to their stated artifacts. This website does not certify every component or claim external accreditation.

title: Research Labs
approach: Quantum-computing, formal-verification, AI-architecture, and governance research materials.
problem: Publish research directions and technical records within the holdings portfolio.
scope: Listed as a holdings research repository. The trust website and its deployment remain separate from SnapKitty infrastructure.

title: Bio-Resonance
approach: A genomic density-operator framework and simulation-oriented modules for research.
problem: Explore the mathematical and computational specification.
scope: Conceptual research only on this website. No clinical validation, diagnostic accuracy, therapeutic efficacy, or regulatory approval is claimed.

title: CPSC
approach: Symmetry admission, translation-orbit checks, Trotter factors, a schedule digest, Q# emission, and a Lean commutation development.
problem: Constrain a periodic transverse-field Ising schedule before emission.
scope: A lattice-model compiler study, not a continuum φ⁴ scattering amplitude. A schedule digest binds content; it is not hardware certification.

title: Unlambda
approach: ATS interfaces, Idris proofs, and SPARK bounded-allocation work.
problem: Build explicit semantics, typed boundaries, and verification gates.
scope: The published scaffold is not a compiler-certified complete Unlambda runtime or a verified generational slot-map heap.
